newsitem.title: USA: Gephardt - New trade pacts must improve on NAFTA.
newsitem.headline: Gephardt - New trade pacts must improve on NAFTA.

text.p: House Democratic Lleader Richard Gephardt said Friday that new trade pacts signed by the United states had to be better than the NAFTA accord with Mexico in dealing with worker and environmental issues.

The Missouri Democrat, who has taken a leading role on trade issues, was responding to a question at a news conference about so-called "fast-track" legislation giving the president authority to negotiate trade agreements.
He said new fast track lesgislation had to deal with environmental issues that had been part of similar trade legislation passed during the George Bush administration.
But he said: "I'm concerned that we simply bring a lot of other countries into a treaty that is exactly like the NAFTA treaty. I think we've got to do better than that."

Gephardt said Chile, seen as a possible NAFTA partner of the United States, was "much ahead" of Mexico and other countries in dealing with labor and environmental concerns, but fast-track legislation "can apply to any number of countries across the board."

"If we are to enter into free trade agreements, I want to be sure, and I think a lot of Democrats want to be sure, that we have taken into account the better approach with regard to enviromental and worker concerns," Gephardt added.
